title: The Nightingale
text:
The Emperor of China learned from a book that the most wonderful thing in his realm was a nightingale that sang in the forest by the sea. No one at court had heard of it. At last a poor girl from the kitchen led the courtiers to the bird, and it came to the palace and sang. The Emperor wept with emotion and kept the nightingale at court.

Then a gift arrived from the Emperor of Japan: an artificial nightingale covered with diamonds, rubies and sapphires, which sang one waltz perfectly every time it was wound. The court adored it. It never tired and was always predictable. While everyone admired it, the real nightingale flew back to the forest, and it was banished from the empire.

One day the mechanical bird broke with a whirr. The watchmaker could repair it only enough for it to be played once a year. Five years later the Emperor fell gravely ill. He lay alone while Death sat on his chest, and he begged the golden bird to sing, but there was no one to wind it.

Suddenly the living nightingale appeared at the window and sang. Death listened, longed for his garden, and drifted away. The nightingale promised to come back and sing to the Emperor about the good and the evil kept hidden from him. When the servants came in to see their dead Emperor, he stood up and said good morning.
lesson: Polished, predictable reports are comfortable, but they cannot tell you what you need to hear. Keep the honest voices close, even if they do not perform on command.
people: The Emperor of China, the nightingale, the kitchen girl
